1. INTRODUCTION

1.1 Background

The development of websites has become an important part of modern business communication and digital marketing. A website enables a business to introduce its products, provide useful information, and help potential customers explore available products through an accessible digital platform.

Sole & Co is a footwear retail website concept designed to help visitors explore shoes for different activities and everyday needs. The website presents three product categories—Sneakers, Running, and Outdoor—along with information about the store, frequently asked questions, and a contact or registration form.

The supplied project is implemented in one HTML file using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The category views are displayed dynamically through URL hash navigation, while the page layout adapts to different screen sizes.

1.2 Project Objectives

1. To create a footwear retail website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

2. To introduce the Sole & Co brand and its footwear categories.

3. To provide navigation from the home page to individual product-category views.

4. To present product names, descriptions, images, and illustrative prices.

5. To provide store information, frequently asked questions, and a customer form.

6. To practice responsive web design and basic front-end interaction.

1.3 Project Scope

The project is a front-end website prototype. It contains a home page and three category views: Sneakers, Running, and Outdoor. The home page also contains About, FAQ, and Contact sections. The supplied source does not include a database, server-side application, real payment feature, or a product-order processing system. The form is therefore presented as a front-end interface and should not be treated as a working account or order service.

2. WEBSITE OVERVIEW

2.1 Website Concept

Sole & Co is presented as a modern footwear store that focuses on comfort, quality, and versatile style. Its visual identity uses a clean layout, neutral backgrounds, dark text, and a warm orange accent color. The home page guides visitors toward the three footwear categories.

2.2 Website Structure

View / SectionHow to accessMain purpose
Home#home or open prototype.htmlIntroduces Sole & Co and links to the main sections.
Sneakers#category-sneakersShows sample everyday sneaker products.
Running#category-runningShows sample running shoes.
Outdoor#category-outdoorShows sample outdoor and hiking shoes.
About#tentangPresents the store's short description and store locations.
FAQ#faqAnswers basic questions about ordering and exchanges.
Contact#kontakProvides a customer form for questions or community registration.

2.3 Technologies Used

HTML5 — Structures the website content, including headings, paragraphs, navigation links, images, product cards, FAQ details, and form controls.

CSS3 — Controls the visual appearance, including colors, typography, spacing, cards, navigation, backgrounds, and responsive layouts.

JavaScript — Handles the menu toggle, reads the URL hash, changes between the home and category views, and creates product cards dynamically.

Web browser — Displays the website and runs its HTML, CSS, and JavaScript code.

3. PAGE-BY-PAGE EXPLANATION

3.1 Home Page

The Home page is the main entry point of Sole & Co. The header displays the Sole & Co brand and a Menu button. The hero section contains the headline “Made for comfort. Easy to love.”, a short description, and an “Explore the collection” button. The collection section introduces Sneakers, Running, and Outdoor as the three main categories.

Further down the page, the About section describes the store's focus on comfort, quality, and versatile design, and displays two store-location labels: Jakarta (Ciplaz Klender Mall) and Bekasi (Mangunjaya Center). The FAQ section contains expandable questions. The Contact section includes fields for a full name, password, shoe size, title, message, and agreement checkbox.

• Introduce the Sole & Co brand and its footwear concept.

• Direct visitors to the three product categories.

• Provide store information and basic customer support information.

• Allow visitors to enter information in the front-end form.

3.2 Sneakers Category View

The Sneakers category is opened by selecting the Sneakers card or navigating to #category-sneakers. JavaScript reads the category key from the URL hash, updates the category title and description, and generates the product cards. The sample products shown in the source are Everyday Court, PUMA IS, and Canvas Low. Each card contains a product image, a short description, and an illustrative price.

• Presents everyday footwear options in a separate category view.

• Uses JavaScript to generate product cards from the category data.

3.3 Running Category View

The Running category is accessed through #category-running. It introduces running shoes and displays three sample products: 910 Haze pro, ORTUSEIGHT X RANK SPORTS, and Harrier. The category description emphasizes comfort and cushioning for everyday running. Product information is rendered dynamically using JavaScript.

• Groups running footwear together for easier browsing.

• Displays product names, descriptions, images, and illustrative prices.

3.4 Outdoor Category View

The Outdoor category is accessed through #category-outdoor. It presents footwear intended for trails, walks, and outdoor activities. The sample products are Trail Explorer, Ridge Hiker, and Pathfinder Mid. Their descriptions refer to traction, cushioning, and ankle support.

• Presents footwear intended for outdoor activities.

• Uses the same product-card layout as the Sneakers and Running views.

3.5 About, FAQ, and Contact Sections

These sections are part of the Home page rather than separate HTML files. The About section introduces the store and shows two location labels. The FAQ uses HTML details and summary elements so visitors can expand or collapse answers. The Contact form collects a visitor's name, password, shoe size, title, message, and consent checkbox.

The supplied form markup includes a POST method but does not specify a server endpoint or backend implementation. Therefore, the current source does not demonstrate persistent account creation, message delivery, or order processing.

4. HTML IMPLEMENTATION

4.1 HTML Page Structure

The source file begins with the HTML5 document declaration and uses the English language setting. The head section contains character encoding, viewport settings, the page title, and a CSS style block. The body contains the site header, main content, category-view container, JavaScript, and footer.

4.2 Navigation and Category Routing

The navigation uses anchor links to page sections. The category cards use hash values such as #category-sneakers, #category-running, and #category-outdoor. JavaScript listens for the hashchange event and displays either the home content or the selected category view. A back link returns visitors to the collection section.

4.3 Content and Form Elements

The HTML uses headings and paragraphs for text, anchor elements for navigation, image elements for category visuals, details and summary elements for FAQ items, and form controls for the customer form. The form includes text and password inputs, a select control, radio buttons, a textarea, a checkbox, and a submit button.

5. CSS IMPLEMENTATION

5.1 CSS Placement

In the supplied prototype.html file, the main CSS rules are written inside a style element in the document head. This is internal CSS. The source also contains selected inline style attributes, for example in the footer paragraph and the form fieldset. No separate external CSS file was included in the uploaded prototype.

5.6 Responsive Design

The stylesheet contains media queries for screen widths of 900 pixels, 700 pixels, and 380 pixels. These rules adjust the number of cards per row, navigation spacing, form padding, footer layout, and other dimensions for smaller screens.

6. JAVASCRIPT IMPLEMENTATION

JavaScript stores the category names, descriptions, and product data in a categories object. When a category hash is detected, the renderRoute() function updates the page title and description, creates product-card elements, hides the home page, and displays the category page. The menu button changes its aria-expanded state and opens or closes the navigation menu. The script also closes the menu when a visitor selects a link, clicks outside the navigation area, or presses Escape.

8. LIMITATIONS

7. The supplied project is a front-end prototype and does not include a backend or database.

8. The contact form does not have a configured server endpoint, so message delivery is not demonstrated.

9. The website does not include a cart, checkout, or real payment process.

10. Product names, descriptions, and prices are sample content; the displayed prices are illustrative.

11. The store-location labels are informational text and are not connected to a map or store-management system.

12. Some footer links are placeholders and do not lead to dedicated policy or social-media pages.

9. CONCLUSION

The Sole & Co project demonstrates a responsive footwear retail website prototype built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It introduces the store, organizes footwear into Sneakers, Running, and Outdoor categories, and provides About, FAQ, and Contact sections. JavaScript supports category navigation and dynamic product-card rendering, while CSS provides the visual design and responsive layout.

The current implementation is limited to the front end. It does not process real purchases, store customer data, or deliver contact messages to a server. Further development could connect the forms and product catalog to a backend system if those functions are required.
